title: Adaptive sparsity routing tracebook
body:
Summary:
This tracebook collects exploratory profiling notes about MoE routing overheads when serving long-context requests across architecture variants (Llama v2-style MLP heads, Mistral-style grouped FFs, and Qwen-style fused kernels). Goal: identify where dynamic gating, scatter/gather, and KV cache interactions dominate latency and memory pressure, and produce low-effort mitigations we can validate in smoke tests.

Context / motivation:
- Recent customer reports show increased p95/p99 tail with sequences >16k tokens when a small fraction of requests hit MoE models.
- Previous profiling focused on steady-state throughput; this doc looks at mixed workloads (variable seq-len, mixed MoE/dense) and routing transients.
- We suspect two hotspots: (1) gating + top-k token routing (CPU + host->device async costs), and (2) uneven expert assignment causing per-expert kernel launch spikes and memory copying.

Experiment setup (single-GPU repro):
- Model variants: llama-moex (16 experts, routing top-2), mistral-moex (8 experts, grouped FF), qwen-moex-copy (12 experts, fused FF kernels where available).
- Hardware: A100-80GB (PCIe), CUDA 12.4, cuDNN 9.x, Triton 2.20 runtime, custom serving-runtime commit SHA: 0a7f3b2.
- Workload: 60% short chat (512 tokens), 30% medium (4k), 10% long (20k). Injected bursts where 6 long requests arrive simultaneously.
- Profiling tools: nsys (full trace), nvprof counters when needed, perf for CPU sampling, and in-service logging (route decisions, per-expert batch sizes).

Runbook (commands used):
- Start nsight trace (ring buffer 60s): 
  nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --capture-range=nvtx --output=moe_routing_burst --sample=none --duration=60s 
- Enable NVTX spans around: request ingestion, gating, scatter, expert-exec start/end, gather, kv-cache read/write, output decode.
- Extract CPU stacks: perf record -F 99 -g -p <pid> -o perf.data 

Key raw observations:
1) Gating wall time: average gating CPU work per request ~0.9ms for short, ~1.8ms for long. Burst gating overheads scale superlinearly when many concurrent long requests (contended mutexes in route table).
2) Host->device submissions: we observed spikes of 3-6ms in CUDA stream synchronization around expert dispatch when expert batch sizes were tiny (<8 tokens). These spikes correspond to stream submissions from different host threads.
3) Expert kernel footprints: Llama-style experts use a heavier GEMM pattern causing higher peak memory but fewer kernel launches (larger kernels). Mistral grouped FFs result in more smaller kernels but better memory locality. Qwen fused kernels are fastest per-op but suffer when dispatch patterns are sparse (low occupancy).
4) KV-cache interaction: long-context reads cause per-token KV cache lookups to dominate memory bandwidth; when combined with MoE gather/scatter the PCIe bus hit rate increases and stalls on other copies. With NVLink-enabled multi-GPU this was less pronounced; PCIe single-GPU setups show bigger tail.
5) Uneven expert imbalance: in burst cases some experts receive tiny microbatches while others are idle; this causes many short-lived kernels and high kernel launch overhead.

Flamegraph and trace highlights (qualitative):
- NVTX spans show gating -> scatter -> expert_kernels -> gather -> kv-cache R/W -> decode. Tail latency aligns with delayed gather completion (waiting on last expert).
- perf stack shows CPU time in hash-based router code (route table lookups + lock contention) and in host-side serialization (flattening indices for scatter/gather).

Quantified numbers (representative, single-run averages):
- p50 latency: dense baseline 46ms, MoE mix 58ms
- p95 latency: dense baseline 132ms, MoE mix 220ms
- p99 latency: dense baseline 315ms, MoE mix 1.07s (burst windows up to 1.8s)
- Average per-expert kernel launch overhead when microbatch<8: ~2.5ms per kernel start (measured as CUDA event gap).

Root-cause hypotheses (short):
A) Host-side routing serialization and mutex contention on the route table for many concurrent requests.
B) Small per-expert microbatches causing kernel-launch dominated execution rather than compute-dominated.
C) KV-cache long-context reads saturating PCIe bandwidth and interfering with scatter/gather copies.
D) Kernel mismatch: some model variants map poorly to available fused kernels, generating many small kernels (Mistral variant alleviates this some).

Quick mitigations to validate (low-effort):
1) Route table redesign: per-worker sharded route maps to avoid global mutex (smoke patch implemented in branch feat/sharded-router). Expected improvement: reduce gating CPU time by ~40–60%.
2) Combine small per-expert microbatches into a coalesced dispatcher on GPU: aggregate microbatches within a 200us window per-expert before launching kernels. Tradeoff: adds bounded latency but reduces kernel launches.
3) KV-cache prefetching and stream prioritization: launch KV reads on dedicated copy streams with higher priority to avoid blocking expert dispatch streams.
4) Fallback knob: if estimated per-expert batch size < threshold, route request to a dense fallback model variant to avoid fragmentation.

Longer-term mitigations / infra changes:
- Persistent kernel queues on GPU: keep a set of pre-initialized CUDA graph captures per-expert to reduce launch overhead. (Complex; requires deterministic shapes or careful graph mutation.)
- Router as a GPU kernel: push gating logic to GPU to avoid host->device roundtrips. Prototype exists in doc/experimental/router-on-device-notes (TODO: convert).
- Dynamic routing policy that considers current expert backlog and KV-cache bandwidth when deciding top-k.

Smoke test plan (what to run after patches):
- Synthetic burst test: 10 long requests arriving in a 200ms window, measure p99 before/after route sharding and coalescing.
- Microbatch histogram: collect per-expert batch size distribution; expect heavier right-tail after coalescing.
- KV bandwidth test: replay long-context read-only traces with and without priority streams to measure stall reduction.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How much added latency will customers tolerate for coalescing microbatches? Need product guidance and SLO thresholds.
- Can we automatically detect when fused kernels are available and prefer model variant A vs B without manual model catalog edits?
- What is the interaction with Dedicated deployments that have NVLink vs Hosted PCIe? Should default configs differ?

Action items (owners):
- Ravi: land route sharding prototype and run the synthetic smoke test (JIRA-ENG-9812). Deadline: 2 weeks.
- Maya: implement microbatch coalescer in the dispatcher and add metrics (per-expert launch count). Deadline: 3 weeks.
- Sofia: KV stream prioritization experiment and benchmark documentation. Deadline: 1 week for initial results.

Notes to self / messy thoughts:
- Observed intermittent "stale" expert assignments where routing table returned stale mapping causing a host-side retry; add versioning to route entries.
- Consider a per-tenant policy: enterprise customers with tight tail requirements can pin to fewer experts or dense variants.
- Need better telemetry: record per-request "routing path" (expert ids) and correlate with p99; store in trace DB but sampled.

Relevant traces / artifacts for follow-up:
- nsys trace: /gs/moe-traces/moe_routing_burst.qdrep (internal storage)
- Perf outputs and flamegraphs: /gs/moe-traces/flame_moe_20241106.tar.gz
- PR with route sharding: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/745

Appendix: example NVTX markers we used (copyable)
- nvtxRangePushA("req-<id>:gating-start"); ... nvtxRangePop();
- nvtxRangePushA("req-<id>:scatter-start");
- cudaEventRecord(start); launch kernels; cudaEventRecord(end); cudaEventElapsedTime(&t, start, end);

Appendix: microbenchmark snippet (pseudo):
- measure_kernel_launch_gap() { 
    for i in 0..N: record cudaEvent, launch no-op kernel, record cudaEvent; measure gaps; 
  }

End.

Document versioning: this is a working tracebook; will iterate after Ravi/Maya experiments.
